exposure: birth setting (freestanding birth centers vs. hospitals)
cohort: The study included 8,738,711 births from low-risk birthing individuals in the United States between 2018 and 2021, with 8,698,432 (99.53%) in hospitals and 40,279 (0.46%) in birth centers.
finding: Neonatal deaths and seizures were not significantly different between freestanding birth centers and hospitals, while chorioamnionitis, Apgar scores < 4, and intensive care admission were less likely to occur in birth centers.
